lease_id.description: Canonical cross-lane lease identifier for the referenced breakglass grant. When present, SHOULD equal grant_id.

grant_digest.description: Optional digest of the breakglass-grant object.

method.description: Concrete access surface actually used for the emergency session. Out-of-band approval or remote-presence transport is not its own session method here: BMC KVM/HTML5 console projects to `console`, Serial-over-LAN projects to `serial`, and virtual-media-assisted recovery reaches breakglass only once a concrete console/serial/ssh session exists. Adapter launch/runtime detail such as remote console URLs, ports, session ids/tokens, plugin/runtime choices, or copied console-entry hints remains redacted side evidence outside the baseline breakglass receipt.

signature.description: Optional detached signature over grant_id + session fields.

notes.description: Optional operator summary text. Do not use `notes` to serialize adapter launch/runtime detail such as remote console URLs, ports, session ids/tokens, image locators, copied ConsoleEntryCommand strings, or other vendor-specific BMC breadcrumbs; those remain redacted side evidence outside the baseline breakglass receipt.

attestation_verification.description: Summary of how attestation evidence affected this authoritative action receipt without making the verifier receipt itself the authority object. For decisive consuming outcomes (`accepted`, `degraded`, `rejected`), pin the exact requirement/receipt/policy digest tuple instead of relying on backend policy-service folklore. `degraded` means the consumed attestation.requirement already allowed degraded posture; v0 has no hidden degraded-waiver lane. Unlike ordinary issue/delivery lanes, breakglass may explicitly record `rejected` because breakglass itself is the already-authoritative emergency lane. Decisive summaries also carry `attestation_receipt_verdict` so the consuming receipt mirrors the exact verdict already present in the pinned `attestation.receipt` rather than reinterpreting it in service-side state. Breakglass now also carries `ordinary_resumption_posture = fresh-attestation-after-breakglass-created-at-required`, which means later ordinary attestation-gated authority must consume a fresh attestation.receipt issued after this breakglass receipt `created_at` instead of reusing pre-breakglass evidence. That post-breakglass ordinary story is time-ordered too: the later ordinary receipt must not predate the fresh attestation receipt it claims to consume.

decision.description: Summary result actually consumed by this authority decision. `attestation_receipt_verdict` must mirror the exact verdict in the pinned attestation receipt; do not reinterpret that verdict in service-side state. `degraded` means the consumed attestation.requirement already allowed degraded posture; v0 has no hidden degraded-waiver lane. Unlike ordinary issue/delivery lanes, breakglass may explicitly record `rejected` because breakglass itself is the already-authoritative emergency lane.

attestation_requirement_digest.description: Exact digest/id of the attestation.requirement actually consumed by this authority decision.

attestation_receipt_digest.description: Exact digest/id of the attestation.receipt actually consumed by this authority decision.

attestation_receipt_verdict.description: Exact verdict from the pinned attestation.receipt. Keep the consuming summary mirror-shaped (`accepted`→`pass`, `degraded`→`degraded`, `rejected`→`fail`) instead of reinterpreting the same receipt in service-side state.

attestation_admission_policy_digest.description: Exact digest/id of the attestation.admission.policy that materially gated this authority decision; do not recover it later from policy-service/database state.

ordinary_resumption_posture.description: Evidence-only reminder that breakglass does not silently reopen ordinary attestation-gated authority. Any later ordinary secret-delivery or workload-identity receipt must consume a fresh attestation.receipt issued after this breakglass receipt `created_at`, and that later ordinary receipt must not predate the fresh attestation receipt it claims to consume, instead of reusing a pre-breakglass accepted/degraded receipt or treating breakglass as standing ordinary authority.

evidence.description: Pointers to stronger evidence emitted during the breakglass session. These artifacts stay evidence-only and do not become the authority object. For the reviewed interactive breakglass shell/console lane, tty recording joins back here and uses tty_recording_start_posture = session-open-before-first-prompt rather than rescue-shell folklore about starting recording later. Richer BMC / virtual-media / serial / console adapter metadata stays redacted side evidence outside the baseline breakglass receipt unless a future dedicated artifact family/RFC says otherwise.

tty_recording_digests.description: Optional digests of tty.session.recording evidence objects emitted for interactive breakglass shell/console sessions.

tty_recording_start_posture.description: If tty recording participates in the reviewed breakglass shell/console lane, capture starts when the session opens and before the first prompt appears; v0 does not bless after-entry manual start as the ordinary reviewed baseline.

kind.description: Exact pre-session recovery-path receipt family that materially enabled this emergency session. The first reviewed join vocabulary stays intentionally small; later richer bootstrap artifacts, if any, need their own follow-on cut.

digest.description: Exact digest/id of the referenced pre-session recovery-path receipt.

bootstrap_receipt_joins.description: Optional exact joins to pre-session recovery-path receipts that materially enabled this breakglass session, such as a reviewed boot override into maintenance or a reset/reprovision authority path. When more than one join is present, list only the enabling receipts in earliest-to-latest order by the joined receipts' own timing instead of mixing in denied attempts, failed dead ends, adapter dashboards, or free-form virtual-media notes. In the common paired one-time-boot case, `boot.override.receipt` appears before the later `reset.receipt` that actuated that next-boot selection. This join is not for post-entry repair receipts.

bootstrap_join_posture.description: If bootstrap_receipt_joins participate, they explain only the recovery-path receipts that occurred before the breakglass session opened. Post-entry repair truth stays on repair_outcome.authoritative_receipt_digests and the referenced authoritative receipts themselves.

bootstrap_join_sequence_posture.description: If bootstrap_receipt_joins participate, the joined receipts are listed only when they materially enabled the actual emergency session, and plural joins appear in earliest-to-latest causal order using the joined receipts' own timestamps. When both a one-time maintenance/recovery boot selection and the reset that actuated it are joined, serialize `boot.override.receipt.applied_at` before the later `reset.receipt.applied_at`/`finished_at` because the override selects the next boot and the reset consumes that selection. Do not include denied attempts, failed dead ends, superseded experiments, or adapter breadcrumbs that did not materially enable the session.

repair_outcome.description: Typed closeout summary for repair work materially attempted under this emergency session. Session exit, transcript availability, or notes do not count as repair proof. Non-observation statuses must carry exact authoritative receipt digests for the derived-operation receipts that prove the attempted repair, confirmation, rollback, or failure state.

authoritative_receipt_digests.description: Exact digests of the authoritative derived-operation receipts (for example config.receipt) that prove the repair attempt or rollback materially performed under this breakglass session.
